classification.difficultyReason: Beyond selecting similarity tests and matching vertices, reject the parallel-line claim by connecting alternate angles to an impossible isosceles triangle, and combine similarity with equal-side markings to recover an unstated whole side.

spec.description: Crossed segments AD and BC, with a right angle between MA and MC; ordinary source blue changed to black under house style.
spec.mathematics: AB=8, AM=6, MC=9, CD=12; AD and BC meet perpendicularly at M. No parallel marks or units.

children.label: i
children.prompt: Prove that $\triangle ABM$ is similar to $\triangle CDM$.

answer.worked:
In triangles $ABM$ and $CDM$, $\angle AMB=\angle CMD=90^\circ$ because the intersecting lines are perpendicular.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{AM}{CM}&=\frac{6}{9}=\frac23\\\frac{AB}{CD}&=\frac{8}{12}=\frac23\end{align*}$$
The hypotenuses and one pair of corresponding sides are proportional. Therefore $\triangle ABM\sim\triangle CDM$ (RHS).
Since $\triangle ABM\sim\triangle CDM$, their matching angles are equal. Hence $\angle ABM=\angle CDM$, so $\angle B=\angle D$.

answer.short: No; the alternate angles are unequal.
answer.worked: If $AB\parallel CD$, alternate angles would give $\angle BAM=\angle CDM$. But similarity gives $\angle CDM=\angle ABM$. This would make triangle $ABM$ isosceles, with $AM=BM$, and hence $AB=6\sqrt2$, contrary to $AB=8$. Therefore $AB$ and $CD$ are not parallel.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{AB}{BD}&=\frac{3}{3/2}=2\\\frac{BC}{DC}&=\frac21=2\\\frac{AC}{BC}&=\frac42=2\end{align*}$$
All three pairs of matching sides have the same ratio. Therefore $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle BDC$ (SSS).

children.label: ii
children.prompt: Which of $\alpha$, $\beta$ and $\gamma$ is equal to $\theta$?

answer.worked: $B$ in triangle $ABC$ corresponds to $D$ in triangle $BDC$. Matching angles of similar triangles are equal, so $\beta=\theta$.

children.label: i
children.prompt: Prove that $\triangle ABC$ is similar to $\triangle CBF$.

answer.worked: $\angle BAC=\angle BCF$ (given). Since $F$ lies on $AB$, $\angle ABC=\angle CBF$ (common angle at $B$). Therefore $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle CBF$ (AAA).

answer.short:
$x=3$, $y=9$.

Use matching sides and the isosceles triangle $BCF$.
answer.worked:
Since $BC=CF$, triangle $BCF$ is isosceles, so $\angle CBF=\angle BFC$. By similarity these correspond to $\angle ABC$ and $\angle ACB$, so $AB=AC=12$.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{BC}{BF}&=\frac{AC}{CF}\\\frac6x&=\frac{12}{6}=2\\x&=3\\y&=AB-BF\\y&=12-3\\y&=9\end{align*}$$
